title: Mitigate token pipeline tethering causing sustained TTFT and tokens/sec collapse across multi-variant routing
creator: Anjali Kapoor
description: Summary: Multiple customers (two enterprise customers and several high-traffic hosted tenants) reported sustained first-token latency regressions and a collapse in tokens/sec for multi-variant requests routed across model families. Symptoms appear as long-running requests that eventually recover but with dramatically reduced throughput for minutes. Scope: observed on Hosted and Dedicated pools and reproduced in a Private (VPC) staging deployment under multi-variant fanout. Root cause hypothesis: under mixed-priority multi-variant routing, per-request KV prefetches and kernel selection heuristics were causing a "tethering" effect: lower-priority requests held prefetch slots while higher-priority requests backed up, triggering repeated kernel selector churn and KV eviction churn that serialized token production. This manifests as high TTFT for affected requests and an overall drop in tokens/sec on the worker. Goal: ship an emergency mitigation that restores baseline TTFT and tokens/sec within the hour for production traffic, then follow with a durable scheduling/eviction fix.
reproduction_steps: 1) Replay customer load profile (mixed model variants: small-ctx + long-ctx + quantized variant) in staging with priority mix 70% normal, 30% high-priority.
2) Enable KV prefetch and kernel-heuristic flags (same defaults as prod).
3) Start steady request storm to simulate tenant fanout and observe first-byte latencies and tokens/sec on affected workers via /metrics and per-route console traces.
4) Inspect logs for repeated kernel-selector decisions and KV eviction events correlated with TTFT spikes.
observed_metrics: TTFT p95 increased from ~120ms -> 900ms on affected workers
tokens/sec on worker dropped by ~6x during peak tethering windows
KV prefetch failure/retry counter spikes (+1800% over baseline)
kernel_selector.swap_count increased, correlated with request timing
router-queue-length for multi-variant paths rose and prioritized requests observed being queued behind low-priority prefetches
mitigation_proposal: 1) Emergency: Introduce a short-term prefetch backoff for concurrent multi-variant requests (configurable circuit-breaker) so a single request cannot occupy multiple prefetch slots for more than 150ms. 2) Router patch: add a soft affordance that prevents low-priority requests from obtaining long-lived prefetch reservations when high-priority requests are queued (priority-aware prefetch gating). 3) Monitoring: add a dedicated alert for kernel_selector.swap_count > threshold and tokens/sec drop > 40% for > 30s. 4) Rollout: Canary patch to 5% of hosted capacity and one Dedicated pool with immediate rollback capability.
detailed_tasks: A. Implement prefetch_backoff circuit-breaker (runtime flag prefetch_backoff_ms) and default to 150ms.
B. Router change: prefer prefetch slot revocation for requests with lower priority when queue pressure detected.
C. Unit & integration tests: add flakiness-tested scenario for multi-variant prefetch starvation.
D. Load test: run k6 profile based on customer traces, validate TTFT and tokens/sec restored to within 10% of baseline.
E. Docs and runbook: update incident runbook with checklist for toggling prefetch_backoff and rolling router policy.
F. Postmortem: collect traces, apply long-term scheduling design in runtime-1.23 planning.
patch_links: https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/1108 - add kernel_selector swap metrics and alert rules
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (Immediate hotfix): Deploy runtime + router hotfix to 5% hosted capacity and a single Dedicated pool (low-risk tenant) during low-traffic window (evening PST). Observe TTFT and tokens/sec for 30 minutes. If stable, increase to 25% and then 75% over 60 minutes. Phase 2 (24h): Expand to remaining capacity and the Private early adopter. Phase 3 (durable): Ship scheduling/eviction redesign in runtime-1.23 with targeted perf regression tests.
testing_plan: - Unit tests for backoff and slot revocation logic. - Integration harness: synthetic multi-variant fanout with priority mixture. - Smoke load test against dedicated staging with production-like traces. - Canary metrics: TTFT p95, tokens/sec per-worker, KV prefetch retry rate, kernel_selector.swap_count.
mitigations_outcome: Canary to 5% showed TTFT p95 drop from 900ms -> 140ms and tokens/sec recovered to 92% of baseline for canary nodes. No increased error rates observed. Continued rollout pending full integration tests.
followups: 1) Design doc for per-worker prefetch quotas and fairness (owner: Marcus Li, due: 2026-03-28).
2) Add deterministic scheduling test to CI to prevent regression (owner: SRE team).
3) Coordinate with Customer Success to notify impacted customers and provide mitigation timeline (owner: Priya Sharma).
